Coalitions

By: Hein Kaiser | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In November 2021 we voted for new councils, and many metros rely on coalition governments to get things done. But are voters getting what they signed up for?

Unique Selling Point:
We have access to the City of Ekurhuleni, notably the worst minority coalition government in SA, and investigate why its simply not working.

Summary:
The Ekurhuleni Council is a mess. It’s coalition government, or what’s left of it, has seen mayor Tania Campbell ousted, then re-elected, and then the speaker ousted, and right now, council is waiting to re-elect a new speaker. The PA and Action SA have both left the coalition, leaving the DA along with a handful of rats and mice parties in power. For how long, nobody knows.

Speaker Raymond Dhlamini was ousted in Ekurhuleni last week, by design of the City Manager who illegally called a council meeting, and illegally got the speaker ousted and replaced by an acting member. City Managers have no executive authority based on the Systems Act (32 of 2000) – they are going to court tomorrow to thrash it out. Dhlamini may be back in office.... and by the time we air the insert, the whole DA led coalition may be gone.

a City Manager acting beyond her paygrade, a crumbling coalition and while service delivery was never spectacular, and lacking in most instances, it’s now much worse.

And while the ANC is no longer in power, for now, in the city, behind the scenes, they are…

Then, the City Manager was appointed by the previous ANC mayor, and most of the heads of department that report to her, too. It’s a legacy municipality with a fresh, previously in opposition coalition.

This is the picture of how a coalition can go terribly wrong on so many levels. And then, the one man band parties, who have as little as a single seat in council, can sway the direction of government, despite the fact that they have no real constituency.



Further information:
- We will be speaking to internal sources who will confirm that the legacy administration was intent on making the coalition fail, especially in terms of service delivery.

- Dhlamini along with Crime Intelligence learnt that his records were fiddled with, by an official in Rustenburg, who changed Dhlamini’s record to reflect criminal charges as opposed to the true story, which was that when he worked as a security guard for Transnet, vagrants were chased off the railways, under command from his superiors at the time. He was never arrested, never in jail, and is South African by birth.

- Service delivery in Ekurhuleni has failed. We evidence two departments and a string of events / examples and incidents.

- We will confront parties that were in, and outside the coalition about the political skullduggery and challenge them about anything being in the best interest of the voters.

The City of Ekurhuleni paints a picture of how badly a coalition with a legacy administration can go wrong - and does this spell potential disaster if a coalition takes over national government in 2024.

Apart from case studies, the insert will make use of a few vox pops to take the story forward.

COALITIONS
SCRIPT
OPENING SEQUENCE
INTRO
Why. Hello there and thank you for joining me as I observe the South African pothole scientifically known as the replaces my tires this every fuckin week as you can see that it is thriving on this stretch of what used to be called road.
VO

Ah yes, the pothole: as much a part of life here as shisanyama, slaptjips, and shutdowns. And a perfect metaphor for the decline of the country’s coalition governments.
Coalitions are inherently fragile, often bringing together political rivals who have little if anything in common. In Italy, their instability has led to close to 70 governments in just 76 years. But the Itlians operate in the national coalition major leagues. Here, we’ve only recently dabbled in them…
…with predictable results.
UPSOUND CORNE MULDER
all our coalitions were to keep the ANC out of power.
VO
Without the luxury of a 51% majority in Gauteng’s 3 metros following the 2021 local elections, opposition parties cozied up to each other. The DA managed to entice Corne Mulder’s Freedom Front and several others into a coalition, and forced the ANC into opposition. Job done for Mulder and co, and a chance for the DA to show what it could do in Jo’burg, Tshwane, and the East Rand’s Ekurhuleni metro.
CORNE MULDER
I think no political party wants to be part of a coalition voluntarily. So it's very nice to govern on your own. And the DA specifically has been used to do that.
VO
But, it didn’t take long for the cracks to show: Jo’burg’s mayor, Mpho Phalatse, hardly had time to decorate her office before being ousted, reinstated, and then ousted again.

And, after a comedy of errors that saw the DA’s Randall Williams resign not once but twice, the Tshwane mayoral chain was handed to a rival coalition only for their candidate to be unmasked as an unrehabilitated insolvent.

Then, just this week, the DA was back at the helm in Tshwane with an entirely new mayor. But, we’d advise you not to blink.

Of the Gauteng coalitions, only Ekurhuleni was left standing - until Thursday.


Council shouting and pushing and shoving here (let it breath and then slowish fade to black)
VO

After a failed first attempt at ousting her, the DA’s mayor, Tania Campbell, faced another motion of no confidence this week. She, too, was given the boot.

And, as in the other two metros, it’s the residents who suffer.


VO

Water shedding… dead traffic lights… refuse removal as regular as a presidential press conference - that is, not regular at all - and, yes, the infamous potholes. Despite the early promise of a Mayor willing to get her hands dirty, service delivery in Ekurhuleni has been the main casualty of the endless political bickering.
LINK
It's like voters are trapped in a political checkmate. Coalition promises of better service delivery have fallen short and citizens are feeling helpless.
VO

And, it seems, local councilors are feeling helpless, too.


UPSOUND SIMON LAPPING
[00:00:12] We here at Benanti Lake in Benoni. And as you can see, we have a wonderful potato farm yet. Oops, sorry. Not a potato farm. This is Hyacinth.


VO

Simon Lapping is from the DA, and is at the sharp end of community frustration. He receives thousands of complaints from irate residents but when orders from above are simply ignored, his hands are tied.


VOX POP WARD CLLR SIMON LAPPING
[00:01:34] The sinkhole which has been four years in the making. Six months ago, Mayor Tania Campbell came out here with the department and gave them instructions for it to be resolved.still nothing has been done.


VO
So, it seems what looked good on paper - a political partnership united against the ANC with a “can-do” mayor at the helm - resulted in a damp squib.
CORNE MULDER

coalitions are under immense pressure. The moment when we got elected the electorate expected us to turn things around from the next day. That's not possible. we inherited in most of those instances, chaos.


VO

Of course, “elected” is the operative word. Coalitions are the result of a divided electorate… and so it’s unsurprising when uncomfortable bedfellows decide to trade in the mattress.

As Ekurhuleni faltered, first the Patriotic Alliance and then ActionSA went in search of somewhere else to lay their heads.

(PAUSE)
VO
Both parties claimed to be fed up with the metro's service delivery shambles. But, the DA was having none of it, instead pointing fingers at the ANC - then in opposition.


FRED NEL
the ANC has deployed cadres within the administration of the municipality.
VO
Fred Nel is the party’s Gauteng Provincial chair.
FRED NEL
And these are all aligned to the ANC. And what they do is if they don't want us to succeed, they just don't deliver the services.
MASA
So are you saying that there's an agenda
FRED NEL
Yes. In order to make our government look bad? Yes
FRED NEL


It does take a long time to turn around some of these municipalities.
MASA

How do you think a resident whose refuse hasn't been picked up, who voted for the DA feels when they hear that?
FRED NEL
If I were a resident, I also don't want to know about the internal politics. I want to have my refuse removed.
VO
Cue the denial. “Not us”, says the ANC.
JONGISIZWE
we did not disrupt them, we did not sabotage them…
VO
Jongisizwe Dhlabati is the leader of the ANC in Ekurhuleni.


JONGISIZWE
… we gave them the benefit of the doubt and all that we did. We became effective in our role of being opposition.
within a short space of time, it became apparent that they are struggling to govern.
VO
Of course, he would say that… except, Carte Blanche has been offered a glimpse of how some in the party view their own record. And, in the battle for hearts and minds, it seems they’re being outmaneuvered.
Voiced messages from the WhatsApp group.








VO
These are actual messages shared between DA Ekurhuleni members on an internal WhatsApp group called - some might say ironically - “SERVICE DELIVERY”
Hardly the sign of a party united in its objective to lead a coalition that delivers on its commitment to the metro’s residents. But, that is not where it ends.
Carte Blanche was sent this message from a DA public representative. It paints a bleak picture of former mayor Tania Campbell’s leadership.
VO

It describes her as dictatorial, saying she makes decisions without consulting anyone.

Concerningly, there are allegations about under-budgeting for pothole repairs because Campbell tried to get an insurance company to foot the bill. They refused, and the roads weren’t fixed.




VO

Signs of a palace revolt are everywhere: earlier this year two DA councillors resigned. One said the job was so stressful it was impacting his health, adding he lacked the necessary support to deliver to his voters.
VO
Philip de Lange, a former DA Ekurhuleni leader, says Campbell is guilty of the very sins the party criticises the ANC for.
MASA
From your experience in leading the Democratic alliance in the city of Ekurhuleni, what is going wrong?
PHILIP
She went and appointed people around her that she was never supposed to appoint.
She's fortified her office, all the mayor’s offices with family and friends.
VO
In an example of that, De Lange hinted that sharing may be….caring.
MASA [11:41:13] What were you able to uncover about jobs for pals and friends
PHILIP [11:41:21] Her daughter, the boyfriend, Josh Seif. He's the boyfriend to her daughter. He's been appointed as the go between in the lead executive.
[11:38:21] Tanya sister's an MP. Michelle Clarke, her daughter, is working in the office of the MCE for corporate inequality since Tanya took over.
[11:41:50] And one of our very close friends outside’s wife Alta De Beer has been appointed as adviser to the embassy for finance.


VO
The City confirmed the employment of both the alleged boyfriend and niece.
FRED NEL
She's allowed to employ whoever she wants in a political office, just like all the other mayors, all and all the other emcees.
MASA
It's not nepotism then.
FRED NEL : No
VO
He sent a message later clarifying that if Campbell’s niece was unfairly appointed there may be an investigation…
We tried to get an interview with then Mayor Campbell, but after 2 requests, she declined and told us to stop asking.


Link
[09:41:13] While the politicians’ bicker, fight and blame each other, it's us ordinary citizens who have to deal with the effects of poor service delivery. Reminding me of that famous African proverb When the elephants fight at the grass, that will be trampled.


VO
And that is why every South African should be paying attention to what happened in Ekurhuleni and Gauteng’s other metros.


ONGAMA
I doubt that the ANC can reverse the tide of electoral losses.



VO
Dr Ongama Mtimkateaches lectures in history and political science at Nelson Mandela University.
MASA
What are the chances that in 2024 we will see single party dominance being an old idea?
ONGAMA
the ANC has been losing support
it may drop below 50%. And as a result of that, we will get a coalition environment.
VO
In other words, what we’re seeing at a local level - in our towns, cities and metros - might be replicated after the provincial and national elections next year. The smart money right now is on an ANC/EFF coalition, but what are the odds on them enjoying more success than what we’re seeing in the metros?
MASA
A year and a bit down the line, do you think voters got what they voted for?
FRED NEL
Voters usually get what they voted for
VO
And in present day South Africa, it’s hard to know if that’s a compliment or an insult.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): In November 2021 we voted for new councils, and many metros rely on coalition governments to get things done. But are voters getting what they signed up for?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have access to the City of Ekurhuleni, notably the worst minority coalition government in SA, and investigate why its simply not working.
metadata.Summary: The Ekurhuleni Council is a mess. It’s coalition government, or what’s left of it, has seen mayor Tania Campbell ousted, then re-elected, and then the speaker ousted, and right now, council is waiting to re-elect a new speaker. The PA and Action SA have both left the coalition, leaving the DA along with a handful of rats and mice parties in power. For how long, nobody knows. Speaker Raymond Dhlamini was ousted in Ekurhuleni last week, by design of the City Manager who illegally called a council meeting, and illegally got the speaker ousted and replaced by an acting member. City Managers have no executive authority based on the Systems Act (32 of 2000) – they are going to court tomorrow to thrash it out. Dhlamini may be back in office.... and by the time we air the insert, the whole DA led coalition may be gone. a City Manager acting beyond her paygrade, a crumbling coalition and while service delivery was never spectacular, and lacking in most instances, it’s now much worse. And while the ANC is no longer in power, for now, in the city, behind the scenes, they are… Then, the City Manager was appointed by the previous ANC mayor, and most of the heads of department that report to her, too. It’s a legacy municipality with a fresh, previously in opposition coalition. This is the picture of how a coalition can go terribly wrong on so many levels. And then, the one man band parties, who have as little as a single seat in council, can sway the direction of government, despite the fact that they have no real constituency.
metadata.Further information: - We will be speaking to internal sources who will confirm that the legacy administration was intent on making the coalition fail, especially in terms of service delivery. - Dhlamini along with Crime Intelligence learnt that his records were fiddled with, by an official in Rustenburg, who changed Dhlamini’s record to reflect criminal charges as opposed to the true story, which was that when he worked as a security guard for Transnet, vagrants were chased off the railways, under command from his superiors at the time. He was never arrested, never in jail, and is South African by birth. - Service delivery in Ekurhuleni has failed. We evidence two departments and a string of events / examples and incidents. - We will confront parties that were in, and outside the coalition about the political skullduggery and challenge them about anything being in the best interest of the voters. The City of Ekurhuleni paints a picture of how badly a coalition with a legacy administration can go wrong - and does this spell potential disaster if a coalition takes over national government in 2024. Apart from case studies, the insert will make use of a few vox pops to take the story forward.
